name: aomega-m3-pretzel-one-dim-reduction
description: Exact one-dimensional reduction of the DG state integral (1202.6268 eq 5.2) at the rank-one quad for 4_1, 5_2 and the (-2,3,7) pretzel: Gaussian coefficient, shifts, mirror form; gates at 4_1 (exact) and 5_2 (mirror of the printed I_{2,3}).

parameters.dictionary: psi_hbar(Z) = Phi_b(c_b - Z/(2 pi b)), hbar = 2 pi i b^2, i pi + hbar/2 = 2 pi b c_b
parameters.fourier: psi^(P) = C^-1 exp[(P^2 + (2 pi i + hbar) P)/(2 hbar)] psi(-P), from DG (C.25) by inversion
parameters.orientation: SnapPy's, for all three; the printed 5_2 form is the mirror

m004.reduced_form: int e^(-1 pi i x^2) Phi_b(1x) Phi_b(1x) dx
m004.prefactor_note: multiply by exp[(i pi + hbar/2)^2 f.B^-1 nu/(2 hbar)] (DG 5.2, f a flattening) and by sqrt(8 pi^3/(hbar^3 det B)) (2 pi hbar)^{-N/2} sqrt(c/(2 pi hbar)) (2 pi i hbar)^{N/2} C^{-N} (1/c) (1/(2 pi b)) e^{pi i c_b^2 Lambda^2/A}; all (5.4)-class up to the hbar power.
m004.exponent_check: A = sum v^2 - 1/c and Lambda = sum v_i (1 - w_i) verified by sympy Poly on the expanded exponent

m015.reduced_form: int e^(-1 pi i x^2) Phi_b(1x) Phi_b(1x) Phi_b(1x) dx
m015.prefactor_note: multiply by exp[(i pi + hbar/2)^2 f.B^-1 nu/(2 hbar)] (DG 5.2, f a flattening) and by sqrt(8 pi^3/(hbar^3 det B)) (2 pi hbar)^{-N/2} sqrt(c/(2 pi hbar)) (2 pi i hbar)^{N/2} C^{-N} (1/c) (1/(2 pi b)) e^{pi i c_b^2 Lambda^2/A}; all (5.4)-class up to the hbar power.
m015.exponent_check: A = sum v^2 - 1/c and Lambda = sum v_i (1 - w_i) verified by sympy Poly on the expanded exponent

m016.prefactor_note: multiply by exp[(i pi + hbar/2)^2 f.B^-1 nu/(2 hbar)] (DG 5.2, f a flattening) and by sqrt(8 pi^3/(hbar^3 det B)) (2 pi hbar)^{-N/2} sqrt(c/(2 pi hbar)) (2 pi i hbar)^{N/2} C^{-N} (1/c) (1/(2 pi b)) e^{pi i c_b^2 Lambda^2/A}; all (5.4)-class up to the hbar power.

verdict: DERIVED (DG 5.2 + C.18 + C.25 + 5.5, GK 1): at a rank-one quad the DG state integral reduces exactly to int e^{-pi i A x^2} prod_i Phi_b(v_i x + sigma_i c_b) dx with A = sum v_i^2 - 1/c and sigma from w = B^-1 nu. 4_1 -> I_{1,2} exactly. 5_2 -> I_{1,3}, NOT the printed I_{2,3}: numerically the two are different functions that are complex conjugates at |b|=1 up to a (5.4)-class unit, i.e. the two ORIENTATIONS of 5_2 (the DG integral on SnapPy's m015 datum is the mirror of the KLV/AK one; A_mirror = 1/c = 2 recovers the printed form). This also explains Part 9's finding that the (1,3) and (2,3) block bilinears coincide. The pretzel (SnapPy orientation): int Phi_b(x)^2 Phi_b(2x - c_b) e^{-2 pi i x^2} dx; mirror: same dilogarithms with e^{-4 pi i x^2 + 4 pi i c_b x}. The doubled factor carries the residual -c_b shift; its poles at c_b + (i b m + i b^-1 n)/2 halve the lattice spacing and the Gaussian cross term e^{pi i m n} couples the q- and q~-halves by parity — the level-2 mechanism, now explicit. Orientation of the derived pretzel integral is SnapPy's and is NOT matched to GGM/GZ's (open, recorded). Next (Part 12): residues at the half-lattice (orders 3 and 1) -> q^{1/2}-series blocks -> sigma_1 sigma_1 index vs the derived index.
